items.title: Harold Danko interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 28, 2021
items.q: I’ve gotten a little bit with Delos, and I’ve gotten awards and whatever you get.

ctx.x: Nineteen, that’s a big plus. And you dealt with basically what I’ll describe as the cream of young musicians. What kind of advice could you give them entering the music field over the years, which you could say I’m not correct in this but it seems like every five or so years certain things go away perhaps to be replaced by something else. But what kind of practical advice could you offer these young people?

Well it’s interesting now because so much has changed in the last year with Covid and everything. And people are finding their way. The students I’m still in touch with are © Fillius Jazz Archive -19-

finding ways to teach on-line, to get their stuff out there in some way. I think the hardest thing is how music seems to be given away. And you know people put it on-line and then it’s up there, it’s like it’s gone you know. And I mean I used to think of like the hopes of an ASCAP royalty, you know whatever, and I’ve gotten a little bit with Delos, and I’ve gotten awards and whatever you get. And it’s not a whole lot. But it’s still something that has your work protected in some way. And the advice that I would…
